3.1.1.2-r1.burton_quote: Love is a voluntary affection, and desire to enjoy that which is good

3.1.1.2-r10.burton_quote: so sweetly and gently win our souls, and strongly allure, that they confound our judgement and cannot be distinguished. Beauty and Grace are like those beams and shinings that come from the glorious and divine Sun, which are diverse, as they proceed from the diverse objects

3.1.1.2-r11.burton_quote: as the species of beauty are taken at our eyes, ears, or conceived in our inner soul

3.1.1.2-r12.burton_quote: And nothing can more please our ears than music, or pacify our minds. Fair houses

3.1.1.2-r14.burton_quote: One Venus is ancient without a mother, and descended from heaven, whom we call celestial; the younger, begotten of Jupiter and Dione, whom commonly we call Venus

3.1.1.2-r15.burton_quote: The one rears to heaven, the other depresseth us to hell

3.1.1.2-r16.burton_quote: the one good, which stirs us up to the contemplation of that divine beauty, for whose sake we perform Justice, and all godly offices, study Philosophy

3.1.1.2-r17.burton_quote: Every creature is good, and may be loved well or ill

3.1.1.2-r18.burton_quote: Two cities make two loves, Jerusalem and Babylon, the love of God the one, the love of the world the other; of these two cities we are all Citizens, as by examination of ourselves we may soon find, and of which

3.1.1.2-r19.burton_quote: One love was born in the sea, which is as various and raging in young men’s breasts as the sea itself, and causeth burning lust: the other is that golden chain which was let down from heaven, and with a divine Fury ravisheth our souls

3.1.1.2-r2.burton_quote: Desire wisheth, Love enjoys; the end of the one is the beginning of the other: that which we love is present

3.1.1.2-r20.burton_quote: a threefold division of this love, which we may use well or ill: God, our neighbour, and the world: God above us, our neighbour next us, the world beneath us. In the course of our desires, God hath three things, the world one, our neighbour two

3.1.1.2-r21.burton_quote: I confound filthy burning lust, with pure and divine Love

3.1.1.2-r22.burton_quote: By this Love (saith Gerson) we purchase heaven, and buy the kingdom of God

3.1.1.2-r3.burton_quote: Love is a desire of enjoying that which is good and fair

3.1.1.2-r4.burton_quote: will not have love to be defined by Desire or Appetite; for when we enjoy the things we desire, there remains no more appetite: as he defines it, Love is an affection by which we are either united to the thing we love, or perpetuate our union

3.1.1.2-r5.burton_quote: All things desire that which is good

3.1.1.2-r6.burton_quote: thou wilt not have bad corn, bad soil, a naughty tree, but all good; a good servant, a good horse

3.1.1.2-r7.burton_quote: No man loves (saith Aristotle 9 mor. cap. 5) but he that was first delighted with comeliness and beauty

3.1.1.2-r8.burton_quote: Beauty is a lively shining or glittering brightness, resulting from effused good, by Ideas, seeds, reasons, shadows, stirring up our minds, that by this good they may be united and made one

3.1.1.2-r9.burton_quote: beauty to be the perfection of the whole composition, caused out of the congruous symmetry, measure, order and manner of parts, and that comeliness which proceeds from this beauty is called grace, and from thence all fair things are gracious
